title: A Rumor in the Class Group Chat
title_ja: クラスのグループチャットに広がるうわさ

source_links.title: UNICEF: Cyberbullying — What It Is and How to Stop It

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: After a school festival, someone sends a message claiming that one student deliberately refused to help clean the classroom.
sentences.ja: 学校祭の後、一人の生徒がわざと教室の清掃を手伝わなかったというメッセージが流れます。

sentences.en: Several classmates forward the message before asking whether the story is accurate or whether something important has been omitted.
sentences.ja: 数人のクラスメートは話が正確か、大切な事情が省かれていないか確かめずに転送します。

sentences.en: However, the student mentioned in the message had been helping a teacher carry equipment to another building.
sentences.ja: しかし名前を挙げられた生徒は教師が機材を別棟へ運ぶのを手伝っていました。

sentences.en: A short online statement can spread faster than the information needed to understand what actually happened.
sentences.ja: 短いオンラインの発言は実際の出来事を理解するのに必要な情報より速く広まることがあります。

sentences.en: Some students feel embarrassed when they realize that they have repeated a claim without reliable evidence.
sentences.ja: 信頼できる証拠なしに主張を繰り返したと気づき、恥ずかしく思う生徒もいます。

sentences.en: The situation shows why group communication involves responsibility as well as the freedom to express opinions.
sentences.ja: この状況はグループ内の意思疎通には意見を表す自由だけでなく責任もあることを示します。

sentences.en: A class representative suggests talking privately with the student before sharing any further claims.
sentences.ja: クラス委員はさらに話を広める前にその生徒と個別に話すことを提案します。

sentences.en: For example, the group could ask an open question about the cleaning schedule rather than accuse anyone of being lazy.
sentences.ja: 例えば誰かを怠け者だと責めるのでなく清掃予定について自由に答えられる質問ができます。

sentences.en: Listening carefully gives a person an opportunity to explain circumstances that others may not know.
sentences.ja: 丁寧に聞くことで他人が知らない事情を説明する機会が生まれます。

sentences.en: The representative also asks classmates not to post screenshots that identify the student without permission.
sentences.ja: 委員は許可なく生徒を特定する画面写真を投稿しないようクラスメートに求めます。

sentences.en: UNICEF advises young people to consider the possible harm of online messages and to seek trusted support when needed.
sentences.ja: UNICEFは若者にオンラインのメッセージによる害を考え、必要に応じ信頼できる支援を求めるよう勧めています。

sentences.en: A respectful response focuses on understanding the situation rather than making an already embarrassed person more uncomfortable.
sentences.ja: 敬意ある対応は恥ずかしい思いをしている人をさらに困らせるのでなく状況の理解を重視します。

sentences.en: The group discovers that simply deleting the original message does not guarantee that every copied version will disappear.
sentences.ja: グループは元の投稿を削除してもすべての複製が消える保証はないと知ります。

sentences.en: In addition, classmates who believed the claim may continue to treat the student unfairly even after the truth is explained.
sentences.ja: さらに事実が説明された後もその話を信じた同級生が不公平に接するかもしれません。

sentences.en: The class therefore discusses how to correct the record without repeating unnecessary personal details.
sentences.ja: そこでクラスは不要な個人情報を繰り返さず事実を訂正する方法を話し合います。

sentences.en: An apology can acknowledge the mistake, but rebuilding trust may require consistent behavior over time.
sentences.ja: 謝罪で間違いを認められますが、信頼の回復には継続的な行動が必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: The teacher reminds students that not every disagreement should become a public argument involving the entire class.
sentences.ja: 教師はすべての意見の違いをクラス全体を巻き込む公開の議論にすべきではないと伝えます。

sentences.en: Careful communication should protect the people involved while allowing a misunderstanding to be corrected.
sentences.ja: 慎重な伝達は誤解を正しながら関係する人々を守るべきです。

sentences.en: The class later creates a short guide about checking claims and responding to hurtful online behavior.
sentences.ja: クラスは後に主張の確認と人を傷つけるオンライン行動への対応について短い案内を作ります。

sentences.en: Students agree that sharing a surprising message can feel exciting when everyone in a group is discussing it.
sentences.ja: 誰もが話題にすると驚くメッセージの共有はわくわくすることがあると生徒たちは認めます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, excitement is not a reliable reason to believe information or pass it to another person.
sentences.ja: それでも興奮は情報を信じたり転送したりする信頼できる理由ではありません。

sentences.en: They decide to pause, examine the source, and ask whether the message could unfairly harm someone.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは投稿前に止まり、情報源と誰かを不当に傷つける可能性を確認することにします。

sentences.en: The most important lesson is not to avoid every difficult conversation but to make room for evidence and empathy.
sentences.ja: 最も重要なのは難しい会話をすべて避けることでなく証拠と共感の余地を作ることです。

sentences.en: Friendship becomes stronger when people are willing to correct mistakes instead of defending every earlier assumption.
sentences.ja: 以前の思い込みをすべて守るのでなく誤りを直そうとすることで友情は強くなります。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Responsible online communication requires verifying claims, respecting others, and correcting mistakes.
Group chats should be closed after festivals.
An apology automatically removes all harm.
questions.explanation_ja: 事実確認・尊重・訂正が主題です。

questions.prompt: What was the student actually doing?
questions.explanation_ja: 生徒は機材運搬を手伝っていました。

questions.prompt: Why should classmates ask before forwarding?
options: Important context may have been omitted from the original message.
Every student wants to be mentioned online.
questions.explanation_ja: 元の情報に欠けた事情があるためです。

options: Speaking privately before making further accusations.
questions.explanation_ja: 公開前に個別で状況を確かめます。

questions.prompt: What does UNICEF encourage young people to consider?
options: The harm online messages may cause and sources of support.
Only how quickly they can type.
The cost of a new phone.
questions.explanation_ja: ネット上での害と信頼できる支援です。

questions.prompt: Why might deletion not end the problem?
options: Copies and unfair impressions may remain.
questions.explanation_ja: 複製や思い込みが残ることがあります。

options: Continuing in a dependable way over time.
questions.explanation_ja: consistentは継続的で一貫したという意味です。

questions.prompt: What does the class guide ask students to do?
options: Check sources and consider whether messages could harm someone.
questions.explanation_ja: 出所と他人への影響を考えます。

questions.prompt: Why isn't excitement a reason to share information?
options: Strong feelings do not prove a claim is accurate or fair.
Sharing is required by school rules.
questions.explanation_ja: 感情と事実の根拠は別だからです。

options: Friends should always defend their first opinions.
Acknowledging errors with evidence and empathy strengthens relationships.
No one should use online messages.
Every disagreement needs a public debate.
questions.explanation_ja: 証拠と共感をもって訂正する重要性です。
